text:
**continue**: land M10, and at the same moment plan a decision for D1. Either land `origin/feat/streamline-doctor-memory` (12 commits, holds the drop box from b52f5b6 / 75a4f41), or ask the owner whether D1 stands. Until then, `kit.py done` refuses every step that changes `kit/board/board_server.py` (7 trunk commits touched it this week).

## Holds
Rerun on branch `m10` at d74d590 (worktree from origin/m10):
- **check**: `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_m10_fix_kinds`: OK.
- **breaks**: the post's `sed` (`FIX_RAISE = 30`): 3 failures. Restored: OK. The check catches a raise that never fires.
- **The orchestrator's start, as it would see it**: `KIT_STALE_OK=1 kit.py resume --role orchestrator` on the m10 checkout opens with "## First: what keeps coming back" and the four lines the post names: "git is the one source" (R1, R2), "never hide an error" (R3, R4), two copies out of sync (6 fixes), silent error (3 fixes). Platform leak (8 fixes) is quiet because it names R5. `kit.py ledger kinds` gives the same counts; `kit.py ledger check`: ok, 25 entries, 0 errors.
- **recheck, bar "His decisions: 4 recorded, 3 with a check; 1 of the 3 fails on the trunk today (the drop box), 1 has none"**: rerun with `scripts/review/CR-m10-a-kind-of-bug-fixed-three-times-becomes-decisions.py` (each decision's check, against the m10 checkout and against `origin/main`): D1 fail, D2 ok, D3 ok, D4 no check. Same on both. I dug into why D1 fails: b52f5b6 (the owner's drop-box commit, 867 lines in board_server.py) is **not an ancestor of main**; it and 75a4f41 live only on `origin/feat/streamline-doctor-memory`, whose board_server.py carries the exact comment D1's check looks for (line 3119). Main's board_server.py has no drop box at all. So the bar is true, and it uncovers something larger than M10: the owner's design has never been on the trunk. CL56 ("an outside AI gets one link ... with the post's drop box", planned) depends on it.

Not checked: the bar "80 of 80 suites" (I did not rerun the whole suite for M10; in this session `tests/test_resume_attached_boards.py` is red on main anyway, see CR-cl58); `done` actually refusing a step (read in `decision_breaks`, not run end to end); the Harmonize run had no ledger, so the raise was never seen on real data there (the post says so).

## Goal
The `memory` train serves "a mistake made once is not made again". M10's measure, a resume line on a seeded ledger, is the right shape: it names what keeps coming back and asks for a check, not a memory line. But the counts are only as good as what gets recorded. The owner said "git is the one source" "about ten times" (the task's own words), and the ledger holds 2, one of them the orchestrator's paraphrase from the task (the post says so under not_checked). Nothing records his chat words automatically. Item 6 asks for decisions "recorded the moment [they are] made, in chat, a comment or a commit"; today that takes a session remembering to run `ledger decide`. That repeats the pattern this step exists to break: a rule that depends on memory.

Seen across posts:
- **Two different M12s.** M10's task item 6 is "merged from M12" (decisions), and its handoff says "what is left of M12 is reading a step's task against them". The board's M12 is now the hand-over hook (CR-m12). That leftover, "a step that contradicts a decision becomes a question", has no post of its own and will be lost under a reused id.
- **Wording nit:** the raised line says "not a fourth patch" for a kind fixed 6 times.

## Verdict
**continue.** The check was rerun and its break seen failing. The orchestrator's start shows the four raised items. The one sampled bar was rerun and holds, and it surfaced a real gap (the owner's drop box never on the trunk). Suggestion: land M10. Before the next step that touches `kit/board/board_server.py` reaches `done`, the orchestrator must settle D1: land `feat/streamline-doctor-memory`, or post the owner a question on whether the drop box stands. Then give "a step that contradicts a decision becomes a question" its own planned step, so it is not lost under the reused M12 id.

Landing: not done from this review session (`kit.py land` was refused here by the session's permission classifier when tried for CL58), so it is left to the orchestrator.
